title: Luke Bible Quiz - Chapter 16
description: Ten questions on Luke 16: the dishonest manager, serving two masters, and the rich man and Lazarus.

questions.text: What accusation was made against the rich man's manager?
questions.explanation: An accusation was made that the manager was wasting his master's possessions.

answers.text: That he was wasting his master's possessions
That he had stolen a hundred cors of wheat
That he refused to collect the debts
That he served two masters

questions.text: What did the manager say he was not able or willing to do?
questions.explanation: The manager said he did not have strength to dig and was ashamed to beg.

answers.text: He could not read his lord's bills
He would not leave his lord's house
He had no strength to dig and was ashamed to beg
He could not collect from the debtors

questions.text: What did the manager tell the debtor who owed a hundred batos of oil to write?
questions.explanation: He told him to take his bill and quickly write fifty.

answers.text: Eighty
Fifty
A hundred
Ten

questions.text: Why did his lord commend the dishonest manager?
questions.explanation: His lord commended the dishonest manager because he had done wisely.

answers.text: Because he had repaid the debts
Because he had given to the needy
Because he had confessed everything
Because he had done wisely

questions.text: What does he say about a servant and two masters?
questions.explanation: He says that no servant can serve two masters, and that you are not able to serve God and Mammon.

answers.text: No servant can serve two masters
A servant may serve two masters in turn
A wise servant serves the richer master
A servant must serve his master's debtors

questions.text: How does the text describe the Pharisees who heard these things?
questions.explanation: The text says the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all these things and scoffed at him.

answers.text: They repented at once and believed him
They were lovers of money and scoffed at him
They asked him for a sign from heaven
They invited him to dine with them

questions.text: How was the rich man in the story clothed?
questions.explanation: The rich man was clothed in purple and fine linen, and lived in luxury every day.

answers.text: In sackcloth and ashes
In the best robe and sandals
In purple and fine linen
In a plain coat

questions.text: What happened to the sores of Lazarus the beggar at the gate?
questions.explanation: Lazarus was full of sores and desired the crumbs from the rich man's table, and even the dogs came and licked his sores.

answers.text: They were washed with oil and wine
They were healed at the gate
They were bound up by the rich man's servants
The dogs came and licked them

questions.text: What did the rich man ask that Lazarus be sent to do for him?
questions.explanation: He asked that Lazarus dip the tip of his finger in water and cool his tongue, because he was in anguish in the flame.

answers.text: Lead him across the great gulf to Abraham
Dip his finger in water and cool his tongue
Carry him away to Abraham's bosom
Bring him purple and fine linen to wear

questions.text: What was the last answer given to the rich man about those who do not listen to Moses and the prophets?
questions.explanation: The answer was that if they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if one rises from the dead.

answers.text: They will repent if a sign is given to them
They will be taught by the angels instead
They will not be persuaded if one rises from the dead
They will be carried to Abraham's bosom too
